assumptions: All graphs and digraphs are finite and simple unless the statement explicitly says otherwise.

definitions.definition: A graph remains connected after deletion of any set of fewer than k edges.
A and B are disjoint edge sets whose union is E(G).
The spanning subgraph of G with vertex set V(G) and edge set A.

domain.description: Finite simple graphs with prescribed edge-connectivity and spanning edge partitions.

quantifiers.domain: partitions E(G)=A⊔B with the stated spanning edge-connectivities

statement.text: For all positive integers a and b, can the edge set of every finite (a+b+2)-edge-connected graph G be partitioned as E(G)=A⊔B so that (V(G),A) is a-edge-connected and (V(G),B) is b-edge-connected?

title: Partitioning edge-connectivity
